title: Finite-map locally free projection and coherent Euler comparison
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $f:X\to Y$ be a finite $k$-morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] between schemes [def-pc-scheme] proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Let $\mathcal E$ be a finite locally free $\mathcal O_Y$-module, meaning Zariski-locally a finite direct sum of copies of $\mathcal O_Y$, with ranks allowed to vary [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf]. Let $\mathcal N$ be any coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Use ordinary module pullback and direct image [def-pc-module-pullback] and sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Then $f^*\mathcal E$ is finite locally free; if $\mathcal E$ is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module], so is $f^*\mathcal E$. The modules $\mathcal E$, $f^*\mathcal E$, $f_*\mathcal N$, $f^*\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal N$, $f_*(f^*\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal N)$ and $\mathcal E\otimes f_*\mathcal N$ are coherent. The canonical projection map
$$\alpha:\mathcal E\otimes_{\mathcal O_Y}f_*\mathcal N\longrightarrow f_*(f^*\mathcal E\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal N),\qquad e\otimes n\longmapsto f^*e\otimes n,$$
is an isomorphism. Here $f^*e$ is the image under the pullback unit. For every $q\ge0$ and $\mathcal G=\mathcal N$ or $f^*\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal N$, the module-cohomology edge map [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]
$$e_{f,\mathcal G}:H^q(Y,f_*\mathcal G)\longrightarrow H^q(X,\mathcal G)$$
[pqf-def-cohomology] is an isomorphism of $k$-vector spaces, where the $k$-actions are through the given structure morphisms. All these cohomology groups are finite-dimensional and vanish for sufficiently large $q$. Thus, for coherent Euler characteristics [def-pc-euler-characteristic],
$$\chi(X,\mathcal N)=\chi(Y,f_*\mathcal N),\qquad \chi(X,f^*\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal N)=\chi(Y,\mathcal E\otimes f_*\mathcal N).$$
No flatness, dominance, dimension or integrality hypothesis is imposed on $f,X,Y$.

proof.text: Choose a trivializing open cover $Y=\bigcup U_i$ and bases $e_{i1},\ldots,e_{ir_i}$ of $\mathcal E|_{U_i}$ [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf]. Put $V_i=f^{-1}U_i$. From the formula $f^*\mathcal E=\mathcal O_X\otimes_{f^{-1}\mathcal O_Y}f^{-1}\mathcal E$ [def-pc-module-pullback], the sections $\eta(e_{ij})=1\otimes e_{ij}$ give a basis on $V_i$: the map $(a_j)\mapsto\sum_j a_j\eta(e_{ij})$ has inverse induced by $a\otimes\sum_j b_je_{ij}\mapsto(a f^\sharp(b_j))_j$. These formulas first apply to inverse-image representatives; changing a representative by restriction does not change them, and the balancing relation identifies $(a f^\sharp(b))\otimes s$ with $a\otimes bs$. They therefore induce mutually inverse maps on the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The $V_i$ cover $X$, so $f^*\mathcal E$ is finite locally free with the same local ranks. When $\mathcal E$ is invertible, take $r_i=1$; the same calculation gives rank-one trivializations of $f^*\mathcal E$, hence it is invertible [def-sc-invertible-module].

A finite locally free module is quasi-coherent and of finite type directly from the affine-local definitions [pqf-def-coherent]: refine each trivializing neighbourhood by affine opens $\operatorname{Spec}A$; the restriction is $\widetilde{A^{r_i}}$, with its $r_i$ standard generators. Apply [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] on the locally Noetherian schemes $Y$ and $X$ to conclude that $\mathcal E$ and $f^*\mathcal E$ are coherent. Since $f$ is finite and $Y$ locally Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-coherent] applied to $\mathcal N$ gives coherence of $f_*\mathcal N$.

For a module $\mathcal M$ on a trivializing open with basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$, the maps $(m_j)\mapsto\sum_j e_j\otimes m_j$ and $(\sum_j a_je_j)\otimes m\mapsto(a_jm)_j$ are inverse, by additivity and balancing. They commute with restriction and hence identify the sheaf tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] with $\mathcal M^{\oplus r}$. Apply this on $V_i$ to $f^*\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal N$, and on $U_i$ to $\mathcal E\otimes f_*\mathcal N$. Restrictions of the coherent factors are coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-module-local-on-open-cover](1); their finite sums are coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-modules-kernel-cokernel-sum](3). Part (2) of the locality node gives coherence of both tensor products. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-finite-pushforward-coherent] applied to the first tensor product gives coherence of $f_*(f^*\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal N)$.

proof.text: Define $\alpha$ first on the presheaf tensor product by $e\otimes n\mapsto\eta(e)\otimes n$. The unit is $\mathcal O_Y$-linear, with the action on $f_*f^*\mathcal E$ restricted along $f^\sharp$ [def-pc-module-pullback]; thus $\eta(ae)\otimes n=f^\sharp(a)\eta(e)\otimes n=\eta(e)\otimes f^\sharp(a)n$. This is balanced, additive in each variable, and compatible with restrictions. The sheafification defining the tensor product [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] gives the displayed global module morphism. For every open $W\subseteq U_i$, the tensor coordinates of Step 3 identify its source sections with $\mathcal N(f^{-1}W)^{r_i}$ and, using the pulled-back basis of Step 1, its target sections with the same module. Its formula sends $e_{ij}\otimes n$ to $\eta(e_{ij})\otimes n$, so it is the identity on these tuples. In particular it is bijective for every such $W$. No assertion that arbitrary tensor-product sections are pure tensors is needed: these identifications are sheaf isomorphisms with finite direct sums, whose sections are finite tuples.

source.place: Tag 01E8 (lemma-projection-formula), final proof paragraph, degree zero: explicit canonical-map and basis calculation

proof.text: For each $y\in Y$ choose $U_i\ni y$. Step 4 gives bijectivity of $\alpha(W)$ on every open $W\subseteq U_i$; [lem-sc-module-hom-local-bijective-iso] therefore makes $\alpha$ an isomorphism. The construction of Step 4 was global, so the local inverses agree on overlaps: if $\beta_i$ and $\beta_j$ are inverse restrictions there, then $\beta_i=\beta_i\alpha\beta_j=\beta_j$. Equivalently a change-of-basis matrix acts on both tuple presentations through the same $f^\sharp$ coefficients. Thus this is the canonical projection map of the statement.

source.place: Tag 01E8 (lemma-projection-formula), final proof paragraph: passage from the free case to a cover

proof.text: For $\mathcal G=\mathcal N$ and for $\mathcal G=f^*\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal N$, coherence has been established; since $X$ is locally Noetherian, [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] makes both quasi-coherent. A finite morphism is affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-cohomology-edge] to $f$ and each $\mathcal G$: the specified edge maps are isomorphisms of $\mathcal O_Y(Y)$-modules, not merely abstract isomorphisms of groups. Restrict scalars along $k\to\mathcal O_Y(Y)$. Because $f$ is a $k$-morphism, the composite $k\to\mathcal O_Y(Y)\to\mathcal O_X(X)$ equals the given structure map of $X$; the resulting maps are therefore isomorphisms for exactly the $k$-vector-space structures in the statement.

source.place: Tag 089W (lemma-relative-affine-cohomology), through 01XC and Cohomology 01F4; scalar restriction along the structure map

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-euler-characteristic-well-defined] on the proper $k$-schemes $X$ and $Y$ to the coherent modules $\mathcal N$, $f^*\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal N$, $f_*\mathcal N$, $f_*(f^*\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal N)$, and $\mathcal E\otimes f_*\mathcal N$. All their cohomology groups are finite-dimensional and zero in sufficiently high degrees. The $\mathcal O_Y$-linear isomorphism $\alpha$ induces $k$-linear isomorphisms on cohomology: apply the cohomology functors [pqf-def-cohomology] to $\alpha$ and its inverse (the derived global-sections functors act on modules over global functions). Step 6 gives equal dimensions for $H^q(X,\mathcal N)$ and $H^q(Y,f_*\mathcal N)$ and, using $H^q(\alpha)$, for $H^q(X,f^*\mathcal E\otimes\mathcal N)$ and $H^q(Y,\mathcal E\otimes f_*\mathcal N)$. Choose a common upper bound for the finitely many nonzero degrees. Sum these termwise equalities with signs $(-1)^q$ using [def-pc-euler-characteristic], obtaining both claimed Euler equalities.
